title: Al-Kawthar 108:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y1 lesson 41 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Kawthar 108:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 41. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ (١) فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ (٢) إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ ٱلْأَبْتَرُ (٣)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], al-Kawthar.
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice [to Him alone].
Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.

keywords.def: a river of great good that Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ
Lord: Allah who looks after us

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Kawthar 108:1-3 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 108:1-3 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Say 'alhamdulillah' for three gifts Allah gave you today.
questions.a: For example: food, my family, my eyes.

questions.q: Al-Kawthar tells us to thank Allah by ...
questions.a: A) praying to Him. 108:2: 'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice [to Him alone].'

questions.q: Al-Kawthar 108:1: «إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ a river in Paradise called Al-Kawthar. What is the best gift you have ever been given, and how did you say thank you?
questions.a: Allah tells us how to say thank you for His gifts: pray to Him and sacrifice for Him (108:2).
